title: The ‘close rule’ finally made wicks click for me. Is this how you actually trade it?
author: Witty_Reaction_9843
selftext:
Day 2 of learning from zero. Yesterday wicks confused me, today it clicked.

The idea is that a level is a price where the market turned before. If a candle’s wick pokes through it but the candle closes back below, that’s a rejection, because price visited but didn’t stay. If the candle actually closes above, that’s a break. I’m learning on D1 and H4 right now. What’s helped is that it animates each candle forming so you can see the wick get pushed back in real time, instead of just staring at a finished chart.

Questions for anyone more experienced: how long do you wait after a close before trusting a break? And does this work the same on lower timeframes or is it mostly noise there?

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
Pretty much how I think about it too. On the waiting part, some people wait for the next candle to hold above the level as well. You give up a bit of price, but it filters a lot of fake breaks.

  
Lower timeframes, yeah, way more noise. A 5m close through a level means a lot less than a daily one. I'd test the rule on the timeframe you actually want to trade before trusting it.
